# Sensitivity to Cross-Border Adjacency {#sec:sensitivity-edges}

The three-country cross-border models include 78 cross-border edges
joining adjacent districts across national borders in the combined
724-district adjacency graph. As a sensitivity check on the contribution
of those edges, Model 4 is refitted with the cross-border edges removed,
leaving only the 1,978 within-country edges. This adjacency-structure
sensitivity follows the recommended practice of [@earnest2007] for
CAR-based disease mapping. Removing the cross-border edges disconnects
the combined graph into three components, one per country; the BYM2
scaling factor [@riebler2016] is recomputed per component and applied per
district following the disconnected-graph treatment of [@freni2018].

## Specification

The edge-deleted model has the same likelihood and linear predictor as
Model 4. The only modification is that the ICAR sum runs over within-country
edges only,
$$p(u \mid W') \propto
  \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{(i,j) \in E_{\text{within}}}(u_i - u_j)^2\right),$$
with per-country sum-to-zero constraints $\sum_{i \in c} u_i = 0$ and a
per-district scaling factor $s'_{c[i]}$ computed from the country
subgraph.

## Within-country edge list and per-country scaling

```{r ed-data, eval = FALSE}
edge_country_a <- all_sf$country[el$node1]
edge_country_b <- all_sf$country[el$node2]
within_mask    <- edge_country_a == edge_country_b

node1_within    <- el$node1[within_mask]
node2_within    <- el$node2[within_mask]
N_edges_within  <- length(node1_within)

compute_scaling_factor_subgraph <- function(node1, node2, n_nodes) {
  A <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = c(node1, node2), j = c(node2, node1),
                             x = 1, dims = c(n_nodes, n_nodes))
  D <- Matrix::Diagonal(x = Matrix::rowSums(A))
  Q <- D - A
  Q_scaled <- INLA::inla.scale.model(
    as(Q, "dgTMatrix"),
    constr = list(A = matrix(1, 1, n_nodes), e = 0)
  )
  exp(mean(log(Matrix::diag(Q_scaled))))
}

country_of_node <- all_sf$country_id
sf_by_country   <- split(seq_len(D_all), country_of_node)
sfac_by_country <- setNames(numeric(3), c("1", "2", "3"))

for (cc in 1:3) {
  nodes_cc <- sf_by_country[[as.character(cc)]]
  mask_cc  <- (el$node1 %in% nodes_cc) & (el$node2 %in% nodes_cc)
  local_id <- setNames(seq_along(nodes_cc), as.character(nodes_cc))
  n1_local <- local_id[as.character(el$node1[mask_cc])]
  n2_local <- local_id[as.character(el$node2[mask_cc])]
  sfac_by_country[as.character(cc)] <-
    compute_scaling_factor_subgraph(n1_local, n2_local, length(nodes_cc))
}

scaling_factor_per_district <- sfac_by_country[as.character(country_of_node)]
```

## Stan model

```{r ed-stan-code}
ed_stan_code <- '
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> T;
  int<lower=1> NT;
  int<lower=1> C;
  int<lower=1> K;

  int<lower=1> N_obs;
  array[N_obs] int<lower=1, upper=NT> obs_idx;
  vector[N_obs] y;
  vector<lower=0>[N_obs] psi;

  array[NT] int<lower=1, upper=N> district;
  array[NT] int<lower=1, upper=T> time;
  vector[NT] year_c;
  array[N] int<lower=1, upper=C> country;

  matrix[NT, K] X;

  int<lower=1> N_edges;
  array[N_edges] int<lower=1, upper=N> node1;
  array[N_edges] int<lower=1, upper=N> node2;
  vector<lower=0>[N] scaling_factor;
}

parameters {
  real mu;
  vector[C - 1] alpha_raw;
  vector[C] delta;
  real delta_bar;
  real<lower=0> sigma_delta;
  vector[N] v;
  vector[N] u_raw;
  real<lower=0> sigma_b;
  real<lower=0, upper=1> phi;
  matrix[C, K] beta_raw;
  vector[K] beta_bar;
  vector<lower=0>[K] tau;
  vector[NT] gamma_raw;
  real<lower=0> sigma_gamma;
}

transformed parameters {
  vector[C] alpha;
  alpha[1] = 0;
  alpha[2:C] = alpha_raw;

  matrix[C, K] beta;
  for (k in 1:K)
    for (c in 1:C)
      beta[c, k] = beta_bar[k] + tau[k] * beta_raw[c, k];

  vector[N] u = u_raw - mean(u_raw);
  vector[N] b = sigma_b * (sqrt(1 - phi) * v
                           + sqrt(phi ./ scaling_factor) .* u);

  vector[NT] gamma_star = sigma_gamma * gamma_raw;

  vector[NT] theta;
  for (n in 1:NT) {
    int d = district[n];
    int c = country[d];
    real xb = 0;
    for (k in 1:K)
      xb += X[n, k] * beta[c, k];
    theta[n] = mu + alpha[c] + b[d]
               + delta[c] * year_c[n]
               + gamma_star[n]
               + xb;
  }
}

model {
  mu ~ normal(-1.85, 1.5);
  alpha_raw ~ normal(0, 1.5);
  delta_bar ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  sigma_delta ~ exponential(5);
  delta ~ normal(delta_bar, sigma_delta);
  sigma_b ~ exponential(4.6);
  phi ~ beta(3, 2);
  v ~ std_normal();
  target += -0.5 * dot_self(u_raw[node1] - u_raw[node2]);
  sum(u_raw) ~ normal(0, 0.001 * N);
  beta_bar ~ normal(0, 1);
  tau ~ exponential(2);
  to_vector(beta_raw) ~ std_normal();
  sigma_gamma ~ exponential(2);
  gamma_raw ~ std_normal();
  y ~ normal(theta[obs_idx], psi);
}

generated quantities {
  vector[N_obs] log_lik;
  for (i in 1:N_obs)
    log_lik[i] = normal_lpdf(y[i] | theta[obs_idx[i]], psi[i]);
}
'

writeLines(ed_stan_code, "fh_bym2_3country_two_time_calyr_edge_del.stan")
```

## Fit

```{r ed-fit, eval = FALSE}
stan_data_edge_del <- stan_data_m4_revised
stan_data_edge_del$node1          <- node1_within
stan_data_edge_del$node2          <- node2_within
stan_data_edge_del$N_edges        <- N_edges_within
stan_data_edge_del$scaling_factor <- scaling_factor_per_district

mod_edge_del <- cmdstan_model("fh_bym2_3country_two_time_calyr_edge_del.stan")
mod_edge_del$check_syntax(pedantic = TRUE)

fit_edge_del <- mod_edge_del$sample(
  data            = stan_data_edge_del,
  chains          = 4,
  parallel_chains = 4,
  iter_warmup     = 1500,
  iter_sampling   = 2000,
  adapt_delta     = 0.97,
  max_treedepth   = 13,
  refresh         = 200,
  seed            = 20260612
)

fit_edge_del <- ensure_fit(fit_edge_del, "m4_edge_del")
```

## Posterior summary

```{r ed-summary}
if (!exists("fit_edge_del") || is.null(fit_edge_del)) {
  fit_edge_del <- restore_fit("m4_edge_del")
}
if (is.null(fit_edge_del)) {
  cat("[ed-summary: no cached fit at output/fits/m4_edge_del.rds; run the fit chunk to populate]\n")
} else {
  param_summary(
    fit_edge_del,
    "Model 4 edge-deletion sensitivity key parameters",
    keep = c("mu", "sigma_b", "phi", "sigma_gamma",
             "alpha", "delta", "delta_bar", "sigma_delta",
             "beta_bar", "tau")
  )
}
```

# Sensitivity Comparison Across Cross-Border Models {#sec:sensitivity-comparison}

The cross-border specifications fitted above explore four modelling
choices in turn: the time-invariance of the BYM2 spatial field (Model 4
versus Model 4a, which lets covariate slopes vary by round), the
contribution of cross-border adjacency (Model 4 versus the edge-deletion
sensitivity), and the assumption of shared BYM2 hyperparameters across
countries (Model 4 versus Model 4b). Each pair is compared by leave-one-out
cross-validation [@vehtari2017] on the expected log predictive density
(ELPD), using the `loo` package implementation. The comparisons within each
block use models fitted to the same observation set, which is the
requirement for LOO-CV comparability.

```{r sensitivity-loo-compare}
# Restore the fits from disk where they are not already in memory.
restore_to_global <- function(fit_var, disk_name) {
  if (!exists(fit_var, envir = .GlobalEnv) ||
      is.null(get(fit_var, envir = .GlobalEnv))) {
    restored <- restore_fit(disk_name)
    if (!is.null(restored)) assign(fit_var, restored, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
}
restore_to_global("fit_m4_revised", "m4_revised_calyr")
restore_to_global("fit_m4a",        "m4a_timevarying_betas")
restore_to_global("fit_m4b",        "m4b_country_bym2")
restore_to_global("fit_edge_del",   "m4_edge_del")

m4_family <- list()
for (nm_label in list(
       c("fit_m4_revised", "Model 4: shared BYM2, full graph"),
       c("fit_m4a",        "Model 4a: time-varying betas"),
       c("fit_m4b",        "Model 4b: country-specific BYM2"),
       c("fit_edge_del",   "Model 4 edge-deletion (within-country only)")
     )) {
  fit_name  <- nm_label[1]
  loo_label <- nm_label[2]
  if (!exists(fit_name) || is.null(get(fit_name))) next
  fit <- get(fit_name)
  if (!"log_lik" %in% fit$metadata()$stan_variables) next
  loo_obj <- tryCatch(fit$loo(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(loo_obj)) m4_family[[loo_label]] <- loo_obj
}

if (length(m4_family) >= 2L) {
  cmp <- loo::loo_compare(m4_family)
  cmp_df <- data.frame(
    Model     = rownames(cmp),
    elpd_diff = round(cmp[, "elpd_diff"], 1),
    se_diff   = round(cmp[, "se_diff"],   1),
    elpd_loo  = round(sapply(m4_family[rownames(cmp)],
                             function(l) l$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"]), 1),
    se_elpd   = round(sapply(m4_family[rownames(cmp)],
                             function(l) l$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"]), 1),
    p_loo     = round(sapply(m4_family[rownames(cmp)],
                             function(l) l$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"]), 1),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )

  knitr::kable(
    cmp_df,
    booktabs = TRUE,
    col.names = c("Model", "ELPD diff", "SE diff", "ELPD", "SE(ELPD)", "p_loo"),
    caption = "Leave-one-out cross-validation across the cross-border two-time models."
  )
} else {
  cat("[sensitivity-loo-compare: fewer than 2 LOO objects available; cannot compare]\n")
}
```

The reading rule for the table is the standard one of [@vehtari2017]: a
difference in ELPD smaller than two standard errors of that difference is
not detectable, and the simpler model in the comparison is preferred on
parsimony grounds.



# External Validation against the Malaria Atlas Project {#sec:map-validation}

The Malaria Atlas Project [MAP; @bhatt2015; @weiss2020] publishes
model-based geostatistical surfaces of *Plasmodium falciparum* parasite
rate for sub-Saharan Africa using a different evidence base and a
different modelling tradition (unit-level point-referenced geostatistics
with continuous-time embedding) than the area-level Fay-Herriot framework
used here. The MAP surfaces provide an external reference against which
the district-level posterior estimates can be compared.

The comparison is framed as **concordance with an independent model**
rather than validation against ground truth, since neither source observes
true district prevalence directly. Two differences in target quantity are
acknowledged explicitly:

- MAP describes an age-standardised parasite rate in children aged two
  to ten years (PfPR$_{2-10}$), whereas the present estimates describe
  RDT positivity in children aged six to fifty-nine months. A level
  offset is therefore expected; the emphasis falls on spatial and rank
  agreement.
- MAP is a continuous-time geostatistical surface fitted to point-level
  data and aggregated; the present estimates are direct area-level
  posteriors. Aggregation noise contributes to any disagreement.
